extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic topology
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of the definitions, basic properties, computational formulas, Adem relations, and algebraic structure of the Steenrod square and power cohomology operations (including applications such as detecting nontrivial stable homotopy and obstructions to splittings, maps, and vector fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology operations ↔ H^n(K(G,m);H) (Proposition 4L.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed m,n,G,H there is a bijection between the set of cohomology operations Θ : H^m(X;G) → H^n(X;H) and H^n(K(G,m);H), given by Θ ↦ Θ(ι) where ι ∈ H^m(K(G,m);G) is a fundamental class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CW approximations and represent classes by maps X→K(G,m). Naturality and associativity of compositions give the correspondence; this is the foundational principle used to construct and classify stable cohomology operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension-decrease/preserve consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohomology operations that decrease degree are trivial because K(G,m) is (m−1)-connected; operations that preserve degree correspond to coefficient homomorphisms via H^m(K(G,m);H) ≈ Hom(G,H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This observation limits possible nontrivial operations and identifies the only degree-preserving operations as those induced by changing coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturality of Sq^i
rubrics_metrics.description: Sqi(f^*(α)) = f^*(Sqi(α)) for any map f : X → Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic functoriality requirement of Steenrod squares; used repeatedly in diagram-chasing arguments and proofs by naturality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additivity of Sq^i
rubrics_metrics.description: Sqi(α + β) = Sqi(α) + Sqi(β).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steenrod squares are additive homomorphisms on cohomology groups with Z2 coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartan formula for Sq^i
rubrics_metrics.description: Sqi(α ∪ β) = Σ_j Sq^j(α) ∪ Sq^{i−j}(β).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This multiplicative compatibility implies the total Sq = Σ_i Sq^i is a ring homomorphism; used to compute action on products and to deduce structure constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension invariance (stability) of Sq^i
rubrics_metrics.description: Sqi(σ(α)) = σ(Sqi(α)) where σ is the suspension isomorphism (given by reduced cross product with generator of H^1(S^1;Z2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability means Sq^i commutes with suspension; contrast: the naive squaring map α ↦ α^2 is not stable because cup products vanish in suspensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Square/degree property and vanishing for Sq^i
rubrics_metrics.description: Sqi(α) = α^2 if i = |α|, and Sqi(α) = 0 if i > |α|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This says Sq^|α|(α) recovers the cup-square for Z2 coefficients and bounds how high Sq^i can act nontrivially on a class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sq^0 = identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation Sq^0 is the identity map on H^*(−;Z2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of axioms (used when forming total Sq).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sq^1 is the Z2-Bockstein
rubrics_metrics.description: Sq^1 equals the Z2 Bockstein β coming from the short exact coefficient sequence 0 → Z2 → Z4 → Z2 → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies Sq^1 with a familiar connecting homomorphism; used to relate odd and even-degree phenomena and to express Sq^{2i+1} = Sq^1 Sq^{2i}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturality of P_i
rubrics_metrics.description: P_i(f^*(α)) = f^*(P_i(α)) for any map f : X → Y (for odd prime p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Steenrod power operations P_i satisfy the same functoriality as Sq^i; analogous statements throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additivity of P_i
rubrics_metrics.description: P_i(α + β) = P_i(α) + P_i(β).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P_i are additive homomorphisms for Z_p coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartan formula for P_i
rubrics_metrics.description: P_i(α ∪ β) = Σ_j P_j(α) ∪ P_{i−j}(β).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total P = Σ_i P_i is a ring homomorphism (with vanishing for large i on any fixed class).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension invariance (stability) of P_i
rubrics_metrics.description: P_i(σ(α)) = σ(P_i(α)) where σ is the suspension isomorphism (reduced cross product with generator of H^1(S^1;Z_p)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P_i are stable operations, commuting with suspension; analogous comments to Sq^i.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power/vanishing property for P_i
rubrics_metrics.description: P_i(α) = α^p if 2i = |α|, and P_i(α) = 0 if 2i > |α| (for odd primes p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identity P_i(α) = α^p can only be expected for even-dimensional α (odd-dimensional α have α^2 = 0 if p odd). Explains the dimension shift 2i(p−1).

rubrics_metrics.name: P^0 = identity
rubrics_metrics.description: P_0 is the identity operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline normalization for the family {P_i}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the Bockstein with P_i
rubrics_metrics.description: The ordinary Bockstein β is not one of the P_i's by convention, but for p = 2 one has Sq^{2i+1} = Sq^1 Sq^{2i} = β Sq^{2i}, so Sq^{2i} play the role of P_i when p = 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep track of β separately for odd primes; it enters Adem relations and algebra generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total operations Sq and P are ring homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Define total operations Sq = Σ_i Sq^i and P = Σ_i P_i; then Sq(α ∪ β) = Sq(α) ∪ Sq(β) and P(α ∪ β) = P(α) ∪ P(β).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only finitely many terms act nontrivially on any fixed class (property (5) ensures finiteness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for Sqi/P_i on powers (projective/lens spaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: For α ∈ H^1(X;Z2): Sqi(α^n) = binom(n,i) α^{n+i}. For α ∈ H^2(X;Zp): P_i(α^n) = binom(n,i) α^{n+i(p−1)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from properties (5) and (6) and the formal identity Sq(α) = α(1+α), P(α) = α(1+α^{p−1}). Use these for explicit computations on RP^∞, CP^∞, HP^∞ and lens spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute binomial coefficients mod p via p-adic expansions (Lucas-type rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If m = Σ m_i p^i and n = Σ n_i p^i are p-adic expansions, then binom(m,n) ≡ Π_i binom(m_i,n_i) (mod p); binom(m,n) is zero mod p if some n_i > m_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to read coefficients in Pascal's triangle mod p and determine which Sqi/P_i terms are nonzero on powers α^n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Steenrod operations to detect/study stable splittings
rubrics_metrics.description: If Steenrod operations tie together powers of a generator (e.g., via the formulas for Sqi(α^n)), then the suspension of the space cannot split stably as a wedge of two spaces with nontrivial cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to RP^∞, CP^∞, HP^∞: the Sq/P relations force all powers of the generator to be linked, obstructing stable splittings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using P_i to constrain degrees of self-maps (HP^∞ degree-square result)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparing P_1(f^*(γ)) with f^*(P_1(γ)) for f:HP^∞→HP^∞ with f^*(γ)=dγ forces congruences d^{(p+1)/2} ≡ d (mod p) for all odd primes p; deduce d is a square (or zero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine action of P_1 on generators with number-theoretic arguments (Legendre symbol, quadratic reciprocity, Dirichlet) to restrict possible mapping degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Sq to bound orthonormal tangent vector fields on spheres
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate existence of k−1 orthonormal tangent vector fields on S^{n−1} to the existence of a map S^{n−1}→RP^{n−1}/RP^{n−k−1} surjective on H^{n−1}(−;Z2); nonvanishing of Sq^{k−1} on the latter forces obstructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose n=2^r(2s+1) and k=2^r+1 to force binomial coefficient parity nonzero, deducing upper bounds on number of vector fields (the classical Adams-type bounds, sharp except in cases handled by K-theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adem relations (general form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relations for compositions: for Steenrod squares (a<2b) Sqa Sqb = Σ_j binom(b−j−1,a−2j) Sq^{a+b−j} Sq^j; for powers (a<pb) P_a P_b = Σ_j (−1)^{a+j} binom((p−1)(b−j)−1, a−pj) P_{a+b−j} P_j, with analogous mixed relations involving β.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adem relations express nonadmissible compositions in terms of compositions with smaller first index; they are the defining relations of the Steenrod algebra and are used algorithmically to reduce monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steenrod algebra A_p: definition, grading and generators
rubrics_metrics.description: A_p is the algebra over Z_p obtained by quotienting the noncommutative polynomial algebra on generators (Sq^i for p=2; β, P_i for odd p) by the two-sided ideal generated by Adem relations (and β^2=0 for odd p). It is graded by degree of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For p=2 the algebra is generated by Sq^{2^k}; for odd p A_p is generated by β and P^{p^k} (Proposition 4L.8 shows most operations are decomposable). H^*(X;Z_p) is an A_p-module for any space X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposability criterion for Sqi/P_i (Proposition 4L.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If i is not a power of 2 then Sq^i can be written as Σ_{0<j<i} a_j Sq^{i−j} Sq^j (so decomposable). Similarly, if i is not a power of p then P_i is decomposable over Z_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses p-adic expansions and choosing a decomposition i=a+b with a< p b so the coefficient of the j=0 term in the relevant Adem relation is nonzero. This identifies the indecomposable generators of A_p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissible monomials and excess
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissible monomials: for p=2 a monomial Sq^{i1} Sq^{i2} ··· is admissible if i_j ≥ 2 i_{j+1} for all j. Define excess e(I)=Σ_j(i_j − 2 i_{j+1}). For odd p admissibility uses inequalities ij ≥ ε_{j+1} + p i_{j+1} with β-exponents ε_j ∈ {0,1}, and excess is defined analogously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissible monomials are those to which no Adem relation applies; excess measures how far a monomial lies above the admissibility threshold and controls when it can act nontrivially on a generator in degree n.

rubrics_metrics.name: H^*(K(Z_p,n);Z_p) generated by admissible monomials of excess < n (main theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each prime p, H^*(K(Z_p,n);Z_p) is the free commutative algebra on elements of the form Θ(ι_n) where Θ ranges over admissible monomials of excess less than n (here ι_n ∈ H^n(K(Z_p,n);Z_p) is the generator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: cohomology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces is freely generated by admissible operations below degree n; consequences include linear independence of admissible monomials and that the stable operations are exactly A_p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence: admissible monomials form a basis for A_p
rubrics_metrics.description: Because H^*(K(Z_p,n);Z_p) is free on admissible Θ(ι_n) for large enough n, admissible monomials are linearly independent and hence form a Z_p-basis for A_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use choose n larger than excesses appearing in any linear relation; evaluation on ι_n then contradicts freeness if relation were nontrivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative (compact) Adem relations
rubrics_metrics.description: An equivalent family of relations: for integers n,k one has Σ_j Sq^{2n−k+j−1} Sq^{n−j} = 0 (and analogues P^{p n−k+j−1} P^n−j = 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These compact relations follow from the Adem relations (and Pascal's triangle) and are sometimes easier to remember/use in computations (special case Sq^{2n−1} Sq^n = 0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic reduction to admissible monomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeatedly apply Adem relations to rewrite any monomial of operations as a sum of admissible monomials; lexicographic ordering ensures termination because each application increases the lexicographic index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the practical computational method for multiplying elements in A_p or evaluating compositions on classes; produces canonical expansion into admissible basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction principle for squares/powers via maps to K(G,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: The construction and verification of Steenrod operations are based on the correspondence between cohomology operations and cohomology classes of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces (see Proposition 4L.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This underpins proofs of basic properties, Adem relations, and the identification of stable operations with elements of A_p; the detailed constructions use CW decompositions and homotopy-theoretic techniques (deferred to later sections).
